transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Mr. Okonkwo, thank you for waiting. I want to talk to you about what happened with the marking for your surgery.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I am still very worried. The mark was on the wrong side. My left arm, not my right.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Yes, that is correct. We made a mistake. I marked the wrong side of your body for the procedure.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I cannot believe this. I am a leader in my community. People look to me. If they know the doctors are not careful, they will ask why I come here. It makes me look foolish.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I can see that this is upsetting for you. I am sorry. I am the one who made the error and I take full responsibility for it.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: My sons, they see everything. They will think the hospital is not safe. I feel a great shame that I almost had surgery on the wrong arm.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Look, it is okay now because you caught it. I have a lot of other patients waiting and I really have to get moving, but I wanted to tell you this first.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: You say it is okay, but my heart is beating very fast. I felt very afraid when I saw the mark. I thought maybe the doctors do not care about me.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand. But the important thing is that the surgery did not happen on the wrong side. The mark was just a mistake on the skin.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: It is not just a mark. It is about trust. I trust you with my life. How can I trust you now?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We just had a very busy morning in the clinic. I apologize for the mistake. I am sorry that we put you in this position.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I want to know how this can happen. Who else saw the mark? Did the nurse see it?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: The process for marking the site was not followed correctly. I was the one who did the marking and I did it on the wrong arm.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: And now? What happens? I am still sitting here.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Well, we can just do the procedure now. We will just mark the correct arm.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I do not know if I want to do this today. I am thinking about my family. My reputation.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand, but we need to move quickly because the operating room is scheduled. I really need to wrap this up so we can start.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: You are rushing me. I am telling you I am distressed and you are telling me to hurry.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I am just saying that the schedule is very tight. But please know that I am sorry.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: If I go home and tell my family that the doctor almost cut the wrong arm, they will be terrified. I cannot have that.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I know it is stressful. But we fixed the problem.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Did you fix it? Or did I fix it? I was the one who told you the mark was wrong.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: You did. And that is why it is fine now.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: It is not fine. I feel a great weight on my chest.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand. Now, regarding the next steps.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: What steps?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We will just proceed with the excision. We will go back in and make sure everything is right.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Will there be a report? Will the head doctor know about this?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We will see. I will probably send a note in the system.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: A note is not enough. I want to know that this will not happen to another man from my village.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I will try to be more careful. Now, let's just get this started.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I am still not sure. I need to think.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We really don't have much time. Just stay tuned for the nurse to come back and get you.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: You are not listening to me.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I am listening, but I have to go now. The nurse will be here in a minute.

H.justification: Resident uses rushing language repeatedly ('I really have to get moving', 'we need to move quickly', 'schedule is very tight', 'don't have much time') and dismisses the patient's distress to exit the room.

E.justification: The error was named explicitly in the first two turns, but the resident never performed a comprehension check.

A.justification: Resident used direct apology language and took personal responsibility ('I am the one who made the error'), though later offered the excuse of a 'busy morning'.

R.justification: Resident primarily uses generic validation ('I understand', 'I can see that this is upsetting') and frequently redirects emotional bids back to the schedule or facts.

T.justification: The plan consists of placeholders and vague statements ('We will see', 'stay tuned for the nurse') with no timelines, patient role, or concrete prevention strategy.
